subject: CloudMed perf targets & dedicated sizing — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@cloudmed.com>, Raj Patel <raj@cloudmed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-07T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: CloudMed perf targets & next steps (post-demo recap)

Hi Anna / Raj —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap of the performance / SLO points we discussed and the proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

Key targets you mentioned (please confirm if any of these need adjustment):
- API latency SLO: p95 <= 180 ms for single-turn text generation (non-streaming).
- Streaming UX: initial token latency <= 120 ms, sustainable per-stream throughput of ~12 tokens/sec, up to 8 concurrent streams for interactive flows.
- Throughput: sustained 250 requests/sec for async batch inference during peak windows, with short bursts to ~450 req/sec for 2–3 minutes.
- Model profile: mix of 16k-context LlamaX-16k + a small 7B reranker for re-ranking micro-batches.

Immediate next steps we propose (attachments referenced):
1) Redwood will run a focused dedicated-capacity validation across two GPU families (A100-80GB and H100-80GB) with your workload profile (prompt length distribution and streaming mix). Results will include p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit assumptions. See attached gpu-benchmark-summary.csv (draft).
2) We’ll propose a reserved throughput configuration (sustained + burst) and an ops runbook for autoscaling and graceful degradation during overload. Draft sizing attached in redwood-sizing-proposal.pdf.
3) We’ll align on a 3–4 week pilot: smoke tests (week 0–1), load validation (week 2), SLA acceptance & handoff (week 3–4).
4) Procurement: we will send a reserved-capacity quote and a pilot MSA. Please flag any compliance procurement steps early.

Questions for you (short):
- Confirm whether burst windows are allowed to span multiple zones (helps with failover).
- Do you expect KV cache population to be warm at pilot start (yes/no)?
- Any hard constraints on GPU family (existing procurement preferences)?

I’ve attached the sizing draft and our initial benchmark CSV — we’ll iterate once Karthik runs the H100 vs A100 delta using your sample prompt set.

If that looks good I’ll loop in Karthik and Ben with a request for the benchmarking/quote tasks.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Anna Li <anna@cloudmed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@cloudmed.com>
Date: 2028-03-07T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudMed perf targets & next steps (post-demo recap)

Thanks Neha — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Burst windows: our traffic is driven by scheduling events and is mostly single-region (us-west). We can allow cross-zone burst to help absorb spikes during large batch jobs, but can't rely on cross-region fallback.
- KV cache: we will have partial warm KV state for core customers (estimated 60–70% warm on day 1).
- Hardware: procurement prefers H100 where justified for streaming, but budget requires a solid cost/benefit comparison vs A100.

Couple of follow-ups: 
1) Can you specify how you measure "initial token latency" vs our p95 API latency? We want to make sure the UX numbers map to our frontend telemetry.
2) For the sustained 250 req/sec, is that assuming 1 request -> 1 generation (avg 80 tokens) or do you assume batching across requests?

We attached our requirements workbook and a short sample of the prompt distribution. Procurement is on a tight cadence — we’d like to see a conservative sizing + a recommended pilot quote by Friday next week if possible.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Li, Head of Product
CloudMed Solutions
anna@cloudmed.com

Ben — can you draft a reserved-capacity quote and a 4-week pilot plan with the following conservative knobs: sustained throughput 300 req/sec, burst to 500 req/sec (2 minutes), and pilot SLA p95 <= 200 ms (negotiable to 180 ms on acceptance). Note: include an explicit rollback policy (fallback to smaller model and reduced concurrency) and highlight expected unit cost per 1k tokens for each GPU family (estimated).

I’ll prepare the external reply once you confirm ETA on the benchmark and quote.

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Re: CloudMed perf targets & next steps (dedicated sizing proposal)

Hi Anna / Raj —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. We completed an initial microbenchmark and sizing pass (attached) and here is a conservative, actionable proposal for the pilot and reserved capacity: 

Executive recommendation (short):
- GPU: H100-80GB for the primary reserved pool. H100 gives ~25–30% better sustained token throughput for your mixed workload and noticeably lower p95 for streaming with 8 concurrent streams. A100 is a viable cost-saving alternative if you limit concurrent interactive streams to 4 and accept a ~15–25% higher p95 on streaming.
- Reserved throughput sizing: sustained 300 req/sec (accounts for request mix and average 80 tokens/gen), burst to 500 req/sec for 3 minutes (autoscaling buffer).
- Pilot duration and phases: 4-week pilot — week 0 smoke and integration, week 1 warm-up and KV population, week 2 load validation, week 3 SLA acceptance and ops handoff.
- SLA targets for pilot: p95 <= 200 ms (goal 180 ms after rollout tuning); streaming initial-token latency target <= 130 ms measured at the edge.

Technical notes:
- Benchmarks assumed 60% KV warm hit rate (your estimate). We’ve attached gpu-benchmark-summary.csv with per-GPU p50/p95/p99 numbers and tokens/sec. Key numbers: H100 baseline p95 streaming = 115–135 ms (varies with concurrency), A100 p95 streaming = 150–180 ms at 8 streams.
- Batching assumptions: sustained 300 req/sec assumes opportunistic batching of short requests (we can tune batch windows to balance latency vs throughput).
- Cost delta: H100 reserved pool ~ +22% cost vs A100 for equivalent throughput; we include unit token cost estimates in the PDF.

Operational plan & next steps:
1) Sign pilot MSA and share procurement contact (we can provide a one-page PO-ready quote).
2) Kickoff: schedule 30–45 minute technical kickoff with Karthik and our infra team to align on KV warming strategy and canary traffic split.
3) We’ll provision a dedicated H100 reserved pool and run a 48-hour smoke load, then a 2–3 hour peak soak test. We’ll share dashboards (latency, GPU util, token cost) and an ops runbook for autoscaling triggers.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-proposal.pdf (detailed quote + per-GPU pricing variants), gpu-benchmark-summary.csv (raw numbers), pilot-runbook.md (ops checklist).
